source.title: The hippocampus as a predictive map

confidence_rationale: Foundational, heavily-cited normative model (validated against place- and grid-cell data) showing that goal-directed navigation is read off the STRUCTURE of a hippocampal representation -- a successor representation whose place fields skew and cluster around rewards and barriers -- rather than off an explicit stored value gradient. This is exactly ARC-057's core thesis ('there is no gradient -- there is more map'). Held at 0.62 because the representational scheme is a successor/predictive map (future-occupancy), NOT REE's DA-modulated RBF density expansion, and the paper contains no separate curiosity/information-seeking drive -- it grounds the 'representation-structure produces approach without an explicit gradient' premise but not the specific SD-024 x SD-025 two-component interaction that ARC-057 asserts.
failure_signatures: The map here is a successor representation encoding expected future state occupancy; place fields reshape around reward/goal locations, but the reshaping is driven by the transition/reward structure of the task, not by a dopaminergic representational-DENSITY expansion signal -- so it supports 'structure not gradient' generically while being silent on the DA-expansion (MECH-232/SD-024) leg ARC-057 specifically invokes.

There is no curiosity or information-seeking drive in the model. Approach follows the value/policy read off the SR map, so the paper does not evidence the ARC-057 claim that a UNIFORM curiosity drive (SD-025) operating on the asymmetrically-shaped map is what converts representational structure into approach.

Because the SR map itself encodes reward-weighted expected occupancy, a critic could argue the map is not gradient-free but rather bakes an implicit value gradient into the representation -- the very implicit/explicit boundary ARC-057 rests on is blurred here.

mapping.source_claim_statement: The firing of hippocampal place cells is well described as encoding a predictive (successor) representation -- expected future state occupancy under the current policy. Place fields skew opposite the direction of travel, cluster and subdivide around rewarded goals and barriers, and grid cells arise as a low-dimensional eigendecomposition of this map. Goal-directed navigation and reward-sensitive reshaping of the representation emerge from the predictive structure of the map itself.
mapping.ree_translation: Grounds the ARC-057 architectural insight that approach behaviour toward reward can be an emergent read-out of representational STRUCTURE rather than a commanded value/wanting gradient. The observation that place fields cluster and subdivide (finer resolution, more sub-fields) around reward locations is the biological analogue of REE's reward-driven representational expansion (MECH-232/SD-024); the fact that navigation is then produced by operating on that shaped map -- not by a separate stored gradient field -- is precisely ARC-057's 'more map, not more gradient' claim.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper's mechanism is a successor/predictive map, not DA-modulated RBF density expansion, and it has no explicit curiosity drive -- so it supports ARC-057's 'representation-structure yields approach without an explicit gradient' premise by functional analogy, not the specific SD-024 x SD-025 interaction. It also arguably folds an implicit value gradient into the SR itself, so the implicit-vs-explicit boundary is softer than in REE. Rodent/human hippocampal model -> REE abstract RBF terrain transfer is by analogy of function.
mapping.source_context: Normative computational model (successor representation / temporal-difference learning) compared against rodent place-cell and grid-cell recordings and human fMRI; simulated spatial navigation in open fields, mazes, and tasks with rewards and barriers.

confidence_components.notes: Foundational high-venue model, strongly validated against neural data. Mapping fidelity moderate: directly supports 'approach from representational structure, no explicit gradient' and the reward-driven field-subdivision analogue of representational expansion, but the representational scheme (SR) differs from RBF density and there is no curiosity-drive component. Transfer risk moderate: hippocampal spatial map -> REE abstract hippocampal RBF terrain, and SR reward-weighting blurs the implicit/explicit gradient line.
